But one of you would draw something, okay? Then the rest of you would see that and draw something else. For example, maybe you draw a sun, then a tree, and another person draws a mountain, almost like telepathy. And that’s how we are: if you put humans in a group, they instantly know how to work together, share ideas, and collaborate. All this stuff is due to intuition. No one said, "Hey, there's a mammoth; let's go kill it for food, housing, and clothing." But walking together, you see a man, and everyone has the same thought: that could be a source of food, clothing, and shelter. You all know how to work together.

The beauty of human imagination and empathy was practiced back then but lost due to civilization. As you can see, humans were very good at working together; no boss needed to say, "Go hunt bisons," "Make clothes," or "Feed kids." Everyone knew exactly what to do without needing communication.

During different times of the year and in various locations, humans formed different organizations. Most of the time, groups of five to ten would go for food. But during religious festivals, hundreds or thousands might gather to celebrate their god. Everything was intuitive; they didn't need communication but knew when a certain organization best fit them.

If you didn’t like the situation, you could go somewhere else and start your own organization. This period in early human history was diverse, dynamic, and creative, though we've forgotten about it. Another example of our creativity are cave paintings from 30,000 to 40,000 years ago. These paintings were beautiful, with a lot of care and devotion put into every detail.

How did they do this? There was no paper or planning; the imagination drove them. They dreamt it, saw the picture in their heads, and drew it on a cave wall to express themselves, leave a legacy, and commemorate animals killed for food, thanking them for the sacrifice by commemorating them. Later, when humans fought battles, they built monuments to celebrate those who fell, creating balance and harmony.

In this world, what matters are these animals because they provide humans with food and clothing. You can see how beautiful these pictures are, how lifelike the animals are. Humans back then had incredible creative potential.
